diagnosis: Repeated actions without meaningful progress are overrepresented in candidate/bad runs, especially repeated clicks, no-ops, and scrolling.
expected_mechanism: A progress check interrupts unproductive loops and forces adaptation. Expected cost: extra state comparison and planning latency, with occasional premature abandonment of a retry that might have succeeded.
policy_text: Before repeating an action, compare the latest state with the state before the prior attempt. If no relevant progress occurred, do not repeat unchanged; diagnose the obstacle and change the action, target, parameters, or strategy. Retry unchanged only with explicit evidence that transient failure is likely.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r '[.stack_frames[0],(.value|tostring)]|@tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '{if($2>0)p[$1]+=$2;else n[$1]+=-$2} END{for(k in p) print k,p[k],n[k],p[k]-n[k]}' | sort -k4,4nr
quantitative_evidence.finding: result:repeated totals 1,485 bad versus 224 good operations: +1,261 bad excess and 6.63× the good count.
Repeated operations are 20.16% of all bad operations (1,485/7,366), versus 5.93% of good operations (224/3,780), a 3.40× normalized overrepresentation.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r 'select(.stack_frames[0]=="result:repeated")|[.labels.comparison_side[0],.labels.source_session[0]]|@tsv' samples.jsonl | sort -u | cut -f1 | sort | uniq -c
quantitative_evidence.finding: Repeated behavior occurs in 88 candidate/bad source sessions versus 20 base/good source sessions, showing recurrence across runs rather than concentration in one trace.
